Abstract
School operations have changed due to information technology. Personalized teaching for preschool children 
requires innovative and adaptable strategies for providing the best-afford experience and learning environment. 
Conventional teaching approaches may not always accommodate students’ learning styles. This can lower perfor-
mance and involvement. The expanding variety of pre-schoolers necessitates creative evaluation and optimization 
methods that promote inclusion and success for all children. The article introduces a preschool teaching evaluation 
model to improve the students’ learning experience. In particular, the evaluation model is designed for various 
assessment strategies irrespective of personalization. The proposed model inputs the students’ learning feasibility 
and the teaching mode to evaluate the personalization adaptability. The fuzzy decision support system improves 
the evaluation based on the above factors. It evaluates student-specific indicators, including attentiveness, body 
language, and engagement, to determine instructional flexibility. The model uses real-time classroom observations 
and student assessments to find realistic approaches with low-to-high fuzzy derivatives. The proposed system 
is designed to compute the adaptability from both factors under low-to-high fuzzy derivatives. By defining the 
maximum feasibility range, the teaching strategy is optimized to meet the adaptability. Thus, the low-level strate-
gies are discarded using adaptability measures to reduce personalization failures. The proposed model is verified 
using adaptability, feasibility, and mode improvements. Research shows that the fuzzy decision support system 
makes courses more adaptive and feasible in many contexts, particularly those that involve games, audiovisual 
approaches, and crafts. Preschoolers, parents, and teachers indicated increased enjoyment, fewer customization 
failures, and greater involvement. Fuzzy-based evaluation increased feasibility ratings and approach versatility. 
The research provides a valuable foundation for solving classroom customization difficulties in preschool set-
tings, emphasizing data-driven, adaptive teaching techniques. This method enables scalable applications in early 
childhood education through fuzzy decision-making and real-time evaluations.
Keywords  Fuzzy decision · Preschool teaching · Strategy evaluation · Teaching personalization
1  Introduction
Personalized teaching strategies are a part of the education approach or process that aims to customize the learn-
ing based on the strengths and weaknesses of the students. The teacher analyses the students’ preferences, skills, 
interests, and strengths [1]. The analyzed features provide potential ideas for personalized teaching strategies.

Technology makes data and analytics easier for teachers to include in their lessons. Instructors who want to 
prepare their students for academic success can use technologies to evaluate their progress in real time or give 
homework feedback. Online platforms allow teachers to produce or choose movies with questions for student 
assignments. Data can assist teachers’ differentiation, student grouping, learning activity scaffolding, and class 
planning. It helps identify youngsters who need guidance and suggests group project leaders. Education deci-
sions using data are more productive, allowing teachers to spend more time with pupils, pay more attention, 
and provide more relevant courses. In addition, the concept of personalized recommendation strategies entails 
making unique recommendations for educational materials and activities based on each student’s strengths and 
interests. Recommendations like this are vital for helping children learn more effectively by exposing them to 
content that is appropriate for their age and stage of development. A personalized teaching strategy is also used 
for preschool students [2]. Preschool students between 2 and 4 are fascinated and energetic over new things 
and activities. Preschool students require a proper personalized teaching strategy, which enlarges the students’ 
extract curricular activity range and skill set [3]. A personalized recommendation strategy is used for preschool 
students. The recommendation strategy uses a collaborative filtering algorithm model to identify the advantages 
and disadvantages of the personalized learning process [4].
Fuzzy decision support systems for early childhood education assessment and improvement are structured and 
adaptable. These methods accommodate student behavior and learning preferences’ volatility. Fuzzy decision 
support systems leverage membership functions and language components to simulate imprecision and facili-
tate complicated decision-making. Fuzzy logic underpins these systems. Fuzzification— transforming raw data 
into fuzzy sets—inference systems, which produce outputs using rules, and defuzzification, which turns fuzzy 
outputs into helpful information, are all vital. FDSS works with confusing data, adapts to learner requirements, 
and improves more personalized outcomes. Rule-based and heuristic decision-making systems are less precise 
and flexible than FDSS. This is because it accounts for pre-schoolers’ complicated and non-linear relationships. 
However, thoroughly comparing it to alternatives like ML systems and integrating these principles may increase 
its classroom value and relevance. The study relies heavily on differentiated teaching strategies, which include 
adapting one’s approach to education and the classroom materials to each student’s unique requirements. By 
promoting an inclusive learning environment, differentiated techniques guarantee that all students, irrespective of 
their starting place, have the chance to succeed. The analyzed features provide proper personalized recommenda-
tions to the pre-schoolers. The recommendation strategy enhances the parents’ satisfaction level, improving the 
students’ skill set [5]. Personalization adaptability is the capacity of educational practices to dynamically modify 
in response to individual student reactions and changing requirements. This versatility is crucial for establishing 
a learning environment that accommodates young learners’ varied learning speeds and preferences, ensuring that 
educational interventions are relevant and successful.
The differentiated teaching strategy is a process that provides tailored instruction to the students to meet their 
individual needs. A differentiated teaching strategy provides instruction over content, process, product, and envi-
ronment [6]. Differentiated teaching strategies are used in preschool to enlarge the skill development range of 
the students. An improved differentiated teaching strategy is used in preschool [7]. The differentiated instruction 
identifies the individual necessities of the students. It helps pre-schoolers’ literacy level, providing optimal skill 
sets and knowledge of the students [8]. The differentiated instruction also enhances the students’ reading, writ-
ing, and oral development range. A differentiated instruction strategy is used in schools to enlarge the learning 
capability of the pre-schoolers [9]. The instruction strategy describes the individual perspectives of the learners. 
The students’ attitudes are analyzed to determine the student’s skill development process. The differentiated 
instruction reduces the latency in understanding the individuality level of the students [10–12].
The fuzzy decision support system uses many rules to construct an application or process. The fuzzy deci-
sion support system is used in the preschool children’s teaching process [13]. The fuzzy decision support system 
is used to improve the accuracy level in the decision-making process. A hybrid fuzzy algorithm-based model 
is used in preschool [14]. The hybrid fuzzy algorithm analyses the critical factors affecting students’ learning 
abilities [15]. The analyzed critical factors provide comprehensive features to enhance the precision level of the

According to the relevant research and case studies, fuzzy decision support systems have demonstrated that 
they are successful and practical in educational contexts. FDSS is effective for measuring the quality of preschool 
programs, with improved judgment accuracy in readiness skill evaluations, as Schmitt et al. [20] showed. In addi-
tion, Hao et al. [21] utilized a fuzzy-based model to improve early childhood teaching strategies. This increased 
instructional accuracy and a subsequent reduction in computational latency. Case studies on hybrid fuzzy algo-
rithms, such as Islam et al. [22], demonstrate that FDSS can dynamically adjust teaching modes, hence addressing 
real-time customization challenges. When dealing with the inherent unpredictability present in early education, 
these examples illustrate how FDSS is more successful than standard heuristic or fixed-rule techniques. This is 
accomplished by offering practical insights and solutions that can be readily implemented. The incorporation of 
these conclusions, which are built on strong groundwork, is what makes this study an improvement to adaptive 
teaching approaches.
With new assessment forms, the suggested approach would allow for a more adaptable and personalized student 
education. To achieve this goal, employ techniques that track students’ engagement, body language, and level of 
focus to develop personalized lesson plans. With fuzzy decision support systems, optimizing instructional strate-
gies by integrating real-time data from the classroom into the model is feasible. Failures in customization will be 
less likely to occur if this is done. Using games and crafts in the class plan can help achieve this goal. Central to 
the concept is that data-driven, adaptable pedagogy should be used in early childhood education settings.
The contributions of this study:
(1)	 improved preschool individualization by creating an evaluation system based on fuzzy logic to continuously 
evaluate and change instructional approaches;
(2)	 implemented a methodical approach to reduce personalizing failures by identifying and discarding low-
adaptability training strategies;
(3)	 used real-time data to validate the suggested approach, showing considerable improvement in student engage-
ment, flexibility, and practicality across different teaching styles.
The rest of the paper is prearranged as follows: Sect. 2 discusses the related works, Sect. 3 proposes the 
preschool teaching evaluation model using a fuzzy decision support system, Sect. 4 deliberates the results and 
discussion and Sect. 5 concludes the research paper.
2  Related Works
Li [23] proposed an interactive teaching evaluation system for preschool education. The proposed system uses 
a machine learning (ML) algorithm that classifies the evaluation’s effects. It is based on the construction of sci-
entific emotion, which analyses the exact teaching abilities of the schools. The proposed system maximizes the 
accuracy of the teaching classification process.
Naji et al. [24] introduced an augmented reality (AR) based system for English teaching in preschools. The AR 
technology provides an immersive interactive learning experience to the learners. A real-time AR-based system 
motivates the learner to learn common concepts and characteristics. The introduced system enlarges the learning 
capabilities of English language learners.
Rahn et al. [25] designed an early childhood teaching approach for preschool English vocabulary. The 
approach is an activity-based intervention that implements vocabulary instruction for the students. Here,

Schmitt et al. [20] proposed a high-quality state-run preschool program evaluation method. The readiness 
skill sets of the students are analyzed to identify the program quality range. The student’s language knowledge 
is also explored during preschool learning. The proposed method minimizes the computational cost level in 
enhancing the teaching abilities of the schools. Experimental results show that the proposed method maxi-
mizes the accuracy of the evaluation.
Chen et al. [27] developed an analysis method for preschool children’s creative and cognitive development 
range. The technique uses a Torrance Test of Creative Thinking (TTCT) data collection tool. The TTCT 
analyses the significance score and ability of the students. This method identifies the impact of the learners’ 
learning abilities. The developed method enhances the student’s creativity and thinking capabilities.
Peretti et al. [28] introduced a technological pedagogical content knowledge (TPCK) framework for pre-
school music learning. The framework is used in Italy to analyze the quality of pre-adolescent education. It 
improves the musical learning abilities of preschool students and reduces the barriers presented during the 
teaching and learning period.
Dikilitaş et al. [29] designed a bilingual education teacher-teaching evaluation method. The method aims to 
analyze the teaching ability of preschool teachers. The trans-language capability and instructional abilities are 
evaluated based on the student’s performance. The method provides proper teaching materials and resources to 
the teachers. The designed method reduces the latency in providing optimal teaching services to the learners.
Xiong et al. [30] proposed a digital educational game for preschool children. The proposed model enhances 
the students’ creative thinking. The game uses a pre-post-test design, providing the students with digitalized 
educational game training. It significantly improves the student’s performance and score ratio. The proposed 
model enlarges the students’ learning abilities compared with other models.
Li et al. [31] developed a quadrilateral evolutionary game model analysis for integrated preschool education. 
The developed analysis model is used to analyze the collaborative behavioral patterns of the learners over 
education. Collaborative governance is evaluated, which provides multiple subjects to the learners. The model 
reduces the latency in the governance evaluation process and increases the accuracy of the analysis process.
Hao et al. [21] designed a deep learning (DL) algorithm-based evaluation method for preschool education. 
The developed method evaluates the effectiveness of educational effects on students. A convolutional neural 
network (CNN) algorithm recognizes education’s optimal effects. The designed method increases the accuracy 
ratio in the effectiveness evaluation process.
Kim [32] proposed a delayed consequences detection model via verbal behavior and delay discounting. 
The incidental bidirectional naming and academic achievements are also used in the model to measure the 
discounting delays. The proposed model reduces the computational cost of providing education services to 
learners and improves the overall tolerance ratio in general education systems.
Wan et al. [33] developed a knowledge diffusion model for personalized educational resource allocation. The 
model uses autonomous learning to allocate educational resources and characterizes the process of knowledge 
diffusion in educational models. It expands the students’ overall scope and learning abilities and improves the 
accuracy of the resource allocation process.
Islam et al. [22] introduced a personalized adaptability knowledge extraction strategy (PAKES) for adaptive 
learning systems. PAKES employs a reinforcement learning algorithm to recommend relevant materials for the

which provides a more detailed knowledge of flexibility throughout a range of low- and high-fuzzy derivatives.
In fuzzy logic, derivatives indicate value changes over time or in response to various situations. The pace 
at which a fuzzy value changes due to changes in settings like teaching methods or exam outcomes is called 
a “fuzzy derivative”. One meaning of the phrase. A fuzzy value is the degree to which a student’s engage-
ment rises or drops over time in response to varied evaluation or teaching methods. This idea may improve 
the assessment of educational techniques’ adaptation to specific students’ requirements. As classroom data 
change, fuzzy derivatives in decision-making models allow the system to adjust its teaching methods. This is 
feasible because the system can adapt. Individualized and adaptable educational methodologies are possible. 
In conclusion, fuzzy derivatives show how fuzzy values evolve, which helps models adapt to students’ learning 
needs and personalize instruction. This method allows for a thorough assessment of how well instructional 
approaches meet the specific needs of every student. The research’s core focus is establishing a maximum fea-
sible range that can be used as a benchmark for improving pedagogical approaches. In cases when educational 
interventions fall short of meeting the needs of specific learners, this optimization is crucial for determining 
which low-level techniques contribute to personalization’s failure. The study aims to improve pre-schoolers’ 
learning experiences and engagement by effectively eliminating these strategies.
Three different differentiation processes are used to enhance children’s focus on learning, which are listed 
below.
(a)	 generating textbooks to learn that improves visual communication among the children;
(b)	 listen to the particular audio file that enhances the student’s ability to listen to the particular topic;
(c)	 involving the sensory perception of movement (i.e.,) body movement that includes the gesture.
From these strategies, the perfect observation is provided to the children in this manner; certain teaching 
techniques are used for the preschool and are given below.
(a)	 provide the student with a choice of learning;
(b)	 mitigate the surrounding;
(c)	 allow for the feedback section;
(d)	 peer teaching;
(e)	 generate the assessment.

5  Conclusion and Future Research Recommendations
Preschoolers’ flexibility and creativity are crucial to individualized learning. Multiple evaluation approaches must 
be used to ensure the strategy’s suitability and benchmarking. This research used fuzzy decision-making to reveal 
a novel evaluation paradigm. This study introduces individualized preschool training using children’s attention, 
posture, and engagement levels as inputs into a fuzzy decision-making model. Examining these components, the 
model adapts educational strategies to each student’s needs. This provides excellent and personalized learning 
experiences for each learner. According to the findings, the fuzzy decision system finds stable adaption feasibility 
options well. It also increases teaching model personalization by addressing incompatibilities between teaching 
approaches and student learning styles. This fuzzy-based method is more flexible and practical than traditional 
approaches. This is because it adapts teaching methods to student engagement and attention. Students study 
better and become more engaged. The study’s conclusions were validated using external datasets and in-depth 
research. This shows that the proposed strategy can increase preschool learning by meeting students’ needs. The

Abstract: School operations have changed due to information technology. Personalized teaching for preschool children requires innovative and adaptable strategies for providing the best-afford experience and learning environment. Conventional teaching approaches may not always accommodate students’ learning styles. This can lower perfor- mance and involvement. The expanding variety of pre-schoolers necessitates creative evaluation and optimization methods that promote inclusion and success for all children. The article introduces a preschool teaching evaluation model to improve the students’ learning experience. In particular, the evaluation model is designed for various assessment strategies irrespective of personalization. The proposed model inputs the students’ learning feasibility and the teaching mode to evaluate the personalization adaptability. The fuzzy decision support system improves the evaluation based on the above factors. It evaluates student-specific indicators, including attentiveness, body language, and engagement, to determine instructional flexibility. The model uses real-time classroom observations and student assessments to find realistic approaches with low-to-high fuzzy derivatives. The proposed system is designed to compute the adaptability from both factors under low-to-high fuzzy derivatives. By defining the maximum feasibility range, the teaching strategy is optimized to meet the adaptability. Thus, the low-level strate- gies are discarded using adaptability measures to reduce personalization failures. The proposed model is verified using adaptability, feasibility, and mode improvements. Research shows that the fuzzy decision support system makes courses more adaptive and feasible in many contexts, particularly those that involve games, audiovisual approaches, and crafts. Preschoolers, parents, and teachers indicated increased enjoyment, fewer customization failures, and greater involvement. Fuzzy-based evaluation increased feasibility ratings and approach versatility. The research provides a valuable foundation for solving classroom customization difficulties in preschool set- tings, emphasizing data-driven, adaptive teaching techniques. This method enables scalable applications in early childhood education through fuzzy decision-making and real-time evaluations.
